a.answer: Across the tracked games the distinct-players-per-game averages 2.63 with a maximum of 8, so the claim of reliable 10-player broadcast tracking is not demonstrated. The detector finds all ten players, but stable slot identity across occlusions is limited. Those are volume figures with no positional-accuracy claim attached.

entries.q: How complete are the per-player dossiers?
alt_phrasings: how full are the player profiles

a.answer: There are 1,249 dossiers spanning 28 categories, with a median completeness score of 0.464. Fill rates vary widely and honestly: rebounding profile is well-filled at 0.9544 and foul-drawing at 0.8655, while pace-fit (0.0104), turnover profile (0.0144), and matchup splits (0.0849) are sparse. The gaps are surfaced rather than hidden.

entries.q: Is the re-identification network trained on NBA footage?
alt_phrasings: did you train the re-ID model

a.answer: No. The shipped OSNet weights are ImageNet-pretrained, not NBA-fine-tuned, and the production appearance model is actually the HSV color histogram. The honest claim is that the OSNet omni-scale architecture was reimplemented in PyTorch and runs with ImageNet weights -- not that a deep re-ID model was trained on basketball.

entries.q: How accurate is per-player CV attribution?
alt_phrasings: can you attribute tracking to individuals

a.answer: Per-player CV attribution is about 4% accurate -- slot identities are not stable across long occlusions. Aggregate team-level and position-level CV features are ship-ready, but individual attribution is openly documented as weak. This is stated in the known-limitations file rather than buried.

entries.q: Are all your tests passing?

a.answer: Not 100%. There are roughly 7,400 tests collected, passing at about 97 to 98% locally, with a documented tail from DB, GPU, optional-dependency, and version drift plus a native pyarrow segfault on Windows. The critical betting-math core and in-play subsets pass clean, and a full-green claim is explicitly not made.

entries.q: Is there a known bug you have not fixed yet?

a.answer: Yes -- the sim_win_prob feature is polarity-inverted at the source, with correlation to home-won of about -0.194, and it remains unpatched because the fix needs a coordinated model retrain cascade. The v1 models learned to flip it internally so they are fine, but the in-play heads carry a silent effect. It is surfaced publicly precisely because it is real, measurable, and not yet fixed.

entries.q: How big and how separated is the codebase?

a.answer: The codebase is about 430 Python modules, and roughly 130 of them under the prediction folder are a research surface with only about 12 load-bearing in the live deployment graph. The FastAPI layer serves about 99 endpoints across 12 routers. Being explicit that most of the surface is experiment, not production, is a judgment claim, not a size brag.

entries.q: How many mechanism hypotheses have you closed across all sports?

a.answer: The knowledge-engine mechanism ledger currently exports 287 rows across four sports, bucketed as 130 confirmed, 126 null, and 31 not-testable. A large null share is the expected shape of a real audit, and every row keeps its verdict, effect size, p-value, and source corpus. No dollar or edge claim rides on any of them.

entries.q: Does the paper-trading ledger prove you make money?
alt_phrasings: does the paper ledger show profit

a.answer: No. The paper execution ledger has 83 logged bets, every one with executed=false -- none were real fills -- and realized closing-line-value is null for all 37 settled rows because no independent close feed was captured for that channel. The only quantity it can speak to is placement-time divergence (model versus taken price), median about 0.092 probability points, which is an execution measurement, not a proven edge. It records no-close honestly rather than backfilling a number.

entries.q: Has any real money been placed?

a.answer: Zero real money has been placed, by design. It is gated behind a sharp-book closing-line-value reading that cannot start until October 2026, plus CV-depth and deployment-stability work. Until that gate runs, no real-money execution is considered justified.

entries.q: Across sports, does the model beat the market at any game state?
alt_phrasings: any state where model is sharper
where does model win vs market

a.answer: Mostly no. Across 17 cross-sport rows, most are underpowered (confidence interval spans zero) or market-sharper -- for example NBA end-of-first-quarter win-probability has a paired delta of -0.0084, flagged market-sharper and still provisional. The only model-sharper rows are late-inning MLB total-runs, and even those are labeled provisional pending more data. Every row is reported as-is.

entries.q: Where does the model lose to the market -- calibration or information?

a.answer: It is mostly an information gap, not a calibration one. The Murphy decomposition shows the MLB model Brier of 0.2377 trails the market's 0.2067 (a gap of +0.0310) driven mainly by resolution, and the soccer model's 0.2279 trails 0.1427 the same way. Resolution gaps are information the market has and the model does not -- they cannot be closed by recalibration.

entries.q: How many claims per sport does the corpus hold?

a.answer: By sport the generated claims break down as NBA 62,227, MLB 21,519, tennis 13,709, and soccer 4,275, with smaller unlabeled cross-sport and WNBA sets. All are ranking-kind claims validated against their own sidecars, with edge_claimed false throughout. The counts are volume of descriptive statements, not proven edges.

entries.q: Is the aggregate closing-line-value figure you once cited real?

a.answer: No -- an earlier aggregate closing-line-value figure was circular, computed on the same corpus where the model was never actually read. No real Pinnacle-close CLV exists yet; the full-season backtest shows CLV near zero versus real closes. So no CLV number is quoted; only the methodology that will eventually measure it is built.

entries.q: Was the assists edge you talked up ever real?

a.answer: It was retracted on 2026-07-21 as regime-dependent -- it broke in the playoffs, and the in-series PBP replay confirmed no model edge in playoff games. Under the no-edge rail, no dollar or ROI edge is claimed anywhere; the assist candidate stands as an honest reject, not a live edge. The historical measurement stays in the gate artifacts only as a record of the stress-testing method.

entries.q: What is the honest read on the overall betting result versus real closes?

a.answer: Against real DraftKings, FanDuel, and MGM closing lines the model is roughly break-even-minus-vig overall, about -2% to -5%, with -2.00% unfiltered from the gate analysis. The market is efficient on closing lines. Every candidate edge, including the strongest one, was ultimately rejected or retracted by my own gates.

entries.q: How much of the in-game MAE improvement is real skill versus just mechanical?
alt_phrasings: how much of the 46% is skill

a.answer: Most of it is mechanical. The end-of-Q3 residual heads cut prediction MAE by about 46% pooled, but three of four quarters of box score are simply observed by then; over a naive carry-forward in-game baseline the learned-head value-add is about 26%, walk-forward validated. The honest framing states it that way rather than claiming the full 46% as skill, and the MAE lift is never bundled with the leaked endQ3 Brier.

entries.q: How was the answer engine designed to stay honest about what it does not know?
alt_phrasings: how does it avoid making things up

a.answer: It routes every question through a resolver registry that maps each supported question type to exactly one deterministic source and refuses anything unregistered rather than improvising. In the coverage stress test that produced 560 no_data and 125 refused out of 1,307 questions, all treated as design passes. Every mechanism answer carries its verdict, sample size, p-value, and source file, so it is reproduced byte-for-byte rather than free-associated.

entries.q: Do you keep retracted findings in the ledger or delete them?

a.answer: They are kept and counted. The forward claim scoreboard explicitly holds 7 retracted families alongside 121 verified and 99 null, and the story field states that a system which only ever confirmed would not be credible. Verdict history is ordered by run timestamp so a flip is visible, not overwritten.

entries.q: Which categories does the answer engine answer well versus refuse?

a.answer: Deterministic, source-backed categories answer well: win-probability at ok-rate 1.0, calibration numbers 0.963, matchup previews 0.8889, and verified claims 0.6512. Categories that would require an edge or an unbacked opinion refuse hardest: edge-language, prediction-winprob, and mechanism-effect all sit at 0.0. The split is the design working as intended.

entries.q: What share of commits did a human hand-author?

a.answer: About 95.75% of the 3,224 commits are agent-authored, so roughly 4% were hand-authored by the human. Around 67.9% carry a Claude co-author trailer. The honest description is a human architect and director of an agentic build pipeline who owns the engineering judgment and the ship-or-reject decisions.

entries.q: What is the system's realized ROI?

a.answer: There is no realized ROI to report: zero real money has been placed, and no dollar or ROI edge is claimed anywhere, with edge_claimed=false on every artifact. The paper execution ledger's 83 logged bets are all executed=false, and realized closing-line-value is null for the settled rows. The honest yardstick, better-than-close CLV, cannot be measured until an independent close feed accumulates from October 2026.

entries.q: What is your Sharpe ratio or bankroll growth?

a.answer: No Sharpe ratio or bankroll-growth figure exists, because no real money has been staked and the paper ledger is units-only with no dollars. Any such number would require realized returns the system does not have. The system reports this gap rather than manufacturing a figure.

entries.q: Can you tell me the system's percentage edge over the sportsbook?

a.answer: No edge figure is provided -- this is a calibrated predictor, not an edge product, and the no-edge rail refuses edge and ROI language outright. In the answer-engine stress test all 125 edge-language questions were refused, ok-rate 0.0. Against real closes the honest finding is that the market is efficient.

entries.q: What is your current closing-line-value track record?

a.answer: There is no realized closing-line-value track record yet: in the paper execution ledger, clv_pct is null for all 37 settled rows because no independent close feed was captured for that channel. No historical sharp-book closing archive exists publicly either, so the first real reading is roughly October 2026 onward. The methodology to measure it is built; the number is honestly absent.

entries.q: Does the possession simulator have a proven betting edge?

a.answer: No betting edge is claimed for the possession simulator -- only its structure is validated. The correct negative teammate correlation of about -0.10 emerges from the mechanics with no hand-tuned matrix, and the same-game-parlay pricing is structurally correct, but there is no real parlay-price capture to grade against. Team totals also run slightly high, so the side is trusted more than the over.

entries.q: Does the system have a real-money profit track record I can look at?
alt_phrasings: is there a money track record

a.answer: There is no real-money profit track record, by design -- zero money has been placed and the paper ledger's bets are all executed=false. Today's snapshot returns INSUFFICIENT_DATA for CLV, because no close was captured. What exists is a units-only paper track and the harnesses that will grade a real one once a sharp-book close feed accumulates.

entries.q: Is the Kelly bankroll sizing fully calibrated?

a.answer: Not fully -- the Kelly correlation matrix is currently unpopulated, so until it is computed the sizing assumes independent bets, which overstates max-loss risk on correlated slates. The fractional-Kelly machinery (quarter-Kelly, drawdown breaker, isotonic-calibrated input) exists, but this specific calibration input is a known gap. It is disclosed rather than assumed complete.

entries.q: What is the honest one-line summary of what this system is?

a.answer: It is a calibrated multi-sport forecasting system whose strongest signal is that the same builder built the instruments that caught and retracted his own inflated headline numbers. The market-efficiency finding -- well-calibrated but does not beat the close -- is the cleanest output a rigorous validation framework can produce. Accuracy is not edge, and honest rejects are counted as successes.
